robot: MyoLeg with an Open-Source Leg prosthesis: a free-standing musculoskeletal human with the right leg's 54 muscles and a knee-ankle prosthesis on the left (MyoSuite, MuJoCo)

frame.base_text: the simulator's world frame (z up): camera poses are given in it; no part here takes an end-effector pose

resets.note: Each episode starts from the same frozen state; only the last episode is graded, and a success ends the run at once.

notes: A muscle's command a sets its excitation u = 1 / (1 + exp(-5 (a - 0.5))), not clipped (a = -1: about 0.0006, a = 0.5: 0.5, a = 1: 0.92); activation follows excitation with a short delay (about 10 ms up, 40 ms down); muscles only pull, one muscle can cross several joints, and its force depends on its length and speed. Before your first command of an episode every column holds -1 (all muscles relaxed). Action type actuators has 56 columns: 0-53 the muscles, 54-55 the prosthesis's knee and ankle torques, which are ignored (the prosthesis's own impedance controller sets them). Every command goes through execute_trajectory space native (action_type actuators, 56 numbers per row). The root (pelvis) is free-standing: its pose and velocity in the world frame are proprio groups root_pose (x y z + wxyz quaternion) and root_vel. The robot's own action type takes one row per control step (the control period is in describe_robot), columns in its layout (describe_robot: action_types_native; spec_file has each actuator, muscle and joint). The state is proprio_now (layout in spec_file: proprio_layout, proprio_groups): joint positions and velocities, muscle activations and lengths, joint efforts. There is no joint-level controller: joints move only through muscle forces. Time passes only inside calls; the service says when the episode ended and why, never the object or goal state.
